summary: All four prior minors are resolved. (1) dueFor now returns 0 for a null, zero or negative value or orderValue. It caps the value with value.min(orderValue), so the share is never more than total and intValueExact() cannot overflow. The result is clamped with Math.max(0, Math.min(share, remaining)), and remaining = Math.max(0, total - prior) is never negative. V5 now has CHECK (redeem_due >= 0 AND earn_due >= 0 AND earn_taken >= 0 AND earn_taken <= earn_due). V5 is unreleased, so editing it is safe. A forged negative or oversized amount can no longer write a negative due or give back more than N or E, and the integration test covers both cases. (2) releaseRedeem (CoinService.java:136) and onFullyRefunded (CoinService.java:178) now subtract priorDue, the sum of per-return dues, under the per-user lock, and write a row only when the remainder is above 0. The legacyAfterPerReturn test confirms totals stay at N and E or below. Re-runs stay idempotent through the ledger unique key. onFullyRefunded subtracts earn_due, not earn_taken, so an earlier shortfall is not recovered later; this matches the documented policy. (3) The non-expiring give-back is written up in the runbook as accepted, consistent with the cancel give-back. (4) The privacy-export follow-up is written up but kept out of the tech-debt register (minor, see above). The delta adds no endpoint, authz change, dependency or secret. The new SQL (priorDue) is parameterised; its only concatenation picks one of two fixed column names. The new warn log and the shortfall log contain only UUIDs and integers. The test-only change to the KafkaJson deserializer adds no attack surface. With no blocker or major findings, the verdict is approve.
